{
  "summary": "The article introduces Tim Costello, a well-known Australian Baptist minister and anti-poverty campaigner. When he was in year 9 at school, he asked whether poverty was just a natural part of life, like the sun rising or the tide going out. He later came to believe that poverty is not natural or unavoidable, but is caused by choices made by governments and society.",
  "simpler_explanation": "Tim Costello has spent much of his life trying to fight poverty. As a teenager, he wondered if poverty was something that simply had to exist. Now, he says poverty happens because of policies and decisions, not because it is inevitable. The article describes him sitting near his home by the beach in Frankston and reflects on his long career. He has worked in poor and disaster-hit areas around the world, served as mayor of St Kilda, written books, and led the charity World Vision Australia for 13 years. He is also often confused with his brother, Peter Costello, who was a Liberal politician and former treasurer.",
  "key_points": [
    "Tim Costello asked an important question about poverty when he was young.",
    "He believes poverty is not natural or unavoidable.",
    "He thinks poverty is caused by policy choices.",
    "He has spent more than 30 years working on poverty and social issues.",
    "He has worked overseas in war zones and disaster areas.",
    "He was mayor of St Kilda and CEO of World Vision Australia.",
    "People sometimes confuse him with his brother Peter Costello, a former politician."
  ]
}
